evidence.claim: The highest federal executive power rests with the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers; the Prime Minister chairs the Council and is Commander-in-Chief of the National Armed Forces, while the President is head of state.
evidence.title: Government | FDRE Office of the Prime Ministers
evidence.publisher: FDRE Office of the Prime Minister
evidence.excerpt: The highest federal executive power rests with the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers; the Prime Minister chairs the Council and is Commander-in-Chief of the National Armed Forces, while the President is head of state.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct government site describing the office structure under Abiy Ahmed's premiership.
evidence.period_fit: Useful as 2022 office baseline even though the page is a current institutional summary rather than a dated 2022 archive.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly identifies Abiy Ahmed's office and the executive/security powers attached to it; this is authority context, not a nuclear-policy act.
contrary_evidence: The page is not a 2022 decision record.
It does not show any nuclear-specific choice.

evidence.claim: The Constitution vests the highest executive powers in the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers, makes them responsible to the House of Peoples' Representatives, and defines the Prime Minister as chief executive, chair of the Council, and Commander-in-Chief of the national armed forces.
evidence.title: The Ethiopia Constitution • Page 27
evidence.excerpt: The Constitution vests the highest executive powers in the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers, makes them responsible to the House of Peoples' Representatives, and defines the Prime Minister as chief executive, chair of the Council, and Commander-in-Chief of the national armed forces.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Legal text with specific executive powers and parliamentary constraints, directly relevant to ruler authority.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Defines Abiy Ahmed's formal authority and constraints; it does not prove any particular 2022 conduct.
contrary_evidence: This is constitutional structure, not performance evidence.
It does not show direct nuclear or existential-risk choices.

evidence.claim: Ethiopia deposited its CTBT ratification on 8 August 2006 and hosts two IMS facilities; the CTBT bans nuclear weapons test explosions and other nuclear explosions.
evidence.title: Ethiopia ratifies Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty
evidence.excerpt: Ethiopia deposited its CTBT ratification on 8 August 2006 and hosts two IMS facilities; the CTBT bans nuclear weapons test explosions and other nuclear explosions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: CTBTO press release directly states Ethiopia's ratification and verification-role status.
evidence.period_fit: Useful inherited baseline for 2022; it shows treaty posture, not a 2022 crisis decision.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State treaty posture, not Abiy personal action; it shows Ethiopia was already committed to the test-ban regime.
contrary_evidence: This does not show command decisions or internal safety governance.
It is a treaty-status fact, not a performance evaluation.

evidence.claim: The Pelindaba status list records Ethiopia as a signatory on 11 April 1996, a ratifier on 18 February 2008, and a deposited party on 13 March 2008.
evidence.title: The African Nuclear-Weapon-Free Zone Treaty (Pelindaba Treaty)
evidence.excerpt: The Pelindaba status list records Ethiopia as a signatory on 11 April 1996, a ratifier on 18 February 2008, and a deposited party on 13 March 2008.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: AU status-list PDF is the treaty registry for African nuclear-weapon-free-zone participation.
evidence.period_fit: Inherited baseline relevant to 2022 because it constrains nuclear posture in Africa.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level treaty baseline, not a personal Abiy action; it shows Ethiopia was within the African nuclear-weapon-free-zone regime.
contrary_evidence: Treaty membership does not prove perfect compliance.
It does not show a 2022 ruler-level nuclear decision.

evidence.claim: Ethiopia has a safeguards agreement in force under the NPT and an Additional Protocol entry for the same safeguards relationship.
evidence.title: Country List : Office of Legal Affairs
evidence.excerpt: Ethiopia has a safeguards agreement in force under the NPT and an Additional Protocol entry for the same safeguards relationship.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: IAEA country factsheet is the authoritative registry for safeguards agreements and protocols.
evidence.period_fit: Useful as a stable legal and institutional baseline for 2022, even though the page is current.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is state-level safeguards status, not a personal policy decision by Abiy Ahmed.
contrary_evidence: Safeguards status does not prove the absence of any hidden risk choices.
It is an institutional constraint, not evidence of active risk reduction by the ruler.
